conventions.producing_part: When several parts give the winning value, the producing part is the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest). Its probability and quote become the combined answer's.
conventions.downgrade_first: Each part's answer is checked (quote, 0.8 bar) before combining; downgraded parts enter as their downgrade target (`unknown`), except page verdicts, which keep their value and the downgraded tag (r2#40).
conventions.missing_tokens: In every order: substantive values > `unknown` > `not_documented`; `not_asked` never competes, because applicability is applied after the gating item is combined.
conventions.combine_gate_items_first: activity_type and action_type (and the scale number) are combined before the items they gate.
conventions.activity_level: Activity items combine the answers about the same activity from every part holding one of its linked passages; parts without a passage do not vote.
conventions.stage6: The same rules apply to pooled Stage 6 evidence split into parts (r2#6); first_section there needs a fixed pool order.

items.basis: Page-level genre: the first part carries the masthead, title and byline that identify who published the page; matches the preset rule for disclosure_form, the sibling page-genre item.
items.probability: The producing (first qualifying) part's chosen-answer probability and quote.
items.downgraded_parts: A downgraded part does not qualify; the next part with a supported substantive answer is used. If none qualifies, `unknown` with the support status of the earliest downgraded part (or `not_documented` if no part stated anything).
items.alternative: highest_probability (the part most confident about the genre).
items.failure_case: A policy-organisation PDF report whose first part is only a cover and table of contents: if part 1 is coded `other` with support, first_section keeps `other` while the body plainly reads as `policy_org`.

items.basis: Metadata, address and archive dates are set once per page, so they need no combining; only the quote-step fallback runs per part. A byline date normally sits at the top, and later parts mostly quote other dates (events, earlier reports). earliest_year would pick referenced past dates.
items.probability: Extractor item, no classifier probability: support is the producing part's quote-presence check (R-042) and, where it applies, the entailment check (R-040, X35).
items.downgraded_parts: A downgraded part does not qualify; the next part with a supported substantive answer is used. If none qualifies, `unknown` with the support status of the earliest downgraded part (or `not_documented` if no part stated anything).
items.alternative: No second type is clearly defensible: highest_probability is unavailable (extractor item) and earliest_year picks referenced past dates.
items.failure_case: A long report with no byline whose only publication statement is a footer 'Published March 2024' in the last part: if part 1's quote step returns an event date as a publication date ('launched on 3 May 2023'), first_section keeps the wrong date.

items.basis: The page's activities are the union of the passages found in every part; links across parts come from segmentation (r2#42: 'segmentation links passages across sections'), using the shared relation list (R-017, r2#22). The ruling names the linking, not the rule type; combined_list is the only one of the six that keeps every passage. Within-part links stay as coded; cross-part links are the segmentation step's own answers.
items.probability: Each passage and each link keeps its own probability; there is no combined value.
items.downgraded_parts: A link coded `unresolved` or downgraded stays `unresolved`; the two passages are kept as separate activities (never merged on a downgraded link).
items.alternative: None of the other five types fits a set of passages.
items.failure_case: A single passage cut by a part boundary mid-sentence ('...the ministry piloted' | 'Copilot for 300 staff') appears as two passages; if segmentation does not link them as the same activity, the page counts two activities, one with a tool and no stage, one with a stage and no tool.

items.basis: Mirrors the ruled page-verdict order (S3 a: confirms_activity > ambiguous_attribution > other_body): own action first, then shared or indirect roles, then unsettled, then another body. Order written for draft 1 (one list). For draft 2 (two linked parts), the relationship part uses this_institution > unit_of_institution > joint_participant > unresolved > other > unknown > not_documented, and the role part is taken from the same part that produced the relationship. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts enter as `unknown` (the downgrade target, R-041), which ranks below every substantive value and above `not_documented`, so any supported answer from another part wins. If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: highest_probability (no ranking of ownership; the part most sure of whose activity it is wins).
items.failure_case: A national program run by an agency for many ministries: part 3 says loosely 'the ministry rolled out the assistant' (`this_institution`); parts 1-2 correctly say `other`. Priority gives `this_institution`, crediting the ministry with another body's activity.

items.basis: Nominal values with no ranking; the activity unit (R-017) makes policy and pilot separate activities, so a conflict between parts about the same activity means one part is wrong, not that both hold. Combined before the items it gates (applicability, r2#8). Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: The winning part's chosen-answer probability and quote (by construction the highest among the supported answers).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts (now `unknown`) are left out of the contest. If all parts are downgraded, `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: priority_order public_facing_service > internal_operational > pilot_experiment > program_initiative > policy_guidance > unknown > not_documented (tool uses before containers, since a part that sees only a program overview tends to give the container value).
items.failure_case: Part 1 is a short summary, 'the city's pilot of a resident chatbot', coded `pilot_experiment` at 0.97; part 2 describes the live public service in detail, coded `public_facing_service` at 0.91. The summary wins.

items.basis: Same reasoning as activity_type: values with no ranking, and a deployment and the governance instrument for it are separate activities (R-017), so cross-part conflict means one part is wrong. Combined before the items gated on it (governed_population, governance_direction). The values are due to be re-ruled (r2#33) before the version steps. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: The winning part's chosen-answer probability and quote (by construction the highest among the supported answers).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts (now `unknown`) are left out of the contest. If all parts are downgraded, `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: priority_order program > governance > deployment > staff_training > unknown > not_documented ('program' is a container used only with named components, and the components may appear only in a later part).
items.failure_case: A named program whose overview is in part 1 ('the AI Assistant Programme gives staff Copilot', coded `deployment` at 0.95) and whose named components are listed in part 2 (`program` at 0.88): highest probability gives `deployment` and the container is lost.

items.basis: Rule type and direction sourced: r2#42 gives 'most advanced stage first' as its example of a per-field order. Proposed within it: `discontinued` first as the terminal stage (it implies earlier use), and the missing-value tokens last. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).

If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: (a) same order with `discontinued` last among substantive values (production > pilot > announced > proposed > discontinued), reading 'most advanced' as most operational; (b) latest-dated stage (the stage the page attaches to its most recent date). (b) is not one of the six ruled types; it would need a seventh type.
items.failure_case: 'The chatbot, in production since 2023, was briefly suspended in March and has since resumed': the part covering the suspension codes `discontinued`, which wins over `production`. Also: the 'permanent pilot' rule (pilot over 12 months with full user base = production) needs facts that can sit in different parts, so no part codes `production` and the combined stage stays `pilot`.

items.basis: Page-stated names, same type as the preset rule for tool and model names; a purchase can have more than one contracting party (consortium; framework plus call-off), so a list loses nothing. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: No single combined probability: each list entry keeps the probability or quote-check result of the part it came from. Extractor item, no classifier probability: support is the producing part's quote-presence check (R-042) and, where it applies, the entailment check (R-040, X35).
items.downgraded_parts: An entry whose quote fails the check is dropped (not listed as `unknown`). If every entry drops, the field is `unknown` with downgraded support status.
items.alternative: first_section (first stated party only), if the column must hold one name.
items.failure_case: Two parts name the same supplier differently ('Microsoft' and 'Microsoft Ireland Operations Ltd'), or one part names the reseller and another the prime contractor: the list shows two parties for one contract.

items.basis: Mirrors tool_name and model_name (preset combined_list): page-stated developers are collected from all parts, and the lookup (with its basis recorded) runs on the combined tool-name list, not part by part. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.

items.downgraded_parts: An entry whose quote fails the check is dropped (not listed as `unknown`). If every entry drops, the field is `unknown` with downgraded support status.

Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.

items.basis: Same structure and reasoning as target_users: widest population first. Combined after action_type, which gates it. items.basis: Conditions first, because a policy with mixed provisions (some uses allowed, some barred) is most often a conditional regime; then prohibits before permits (binding limits before allowances). Depends on the draft value list, including whether 'requires or promotes' is one value or two. Combined after action_type. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).

If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: (a) most restrictive first: prohibits > restricts_with_conditions > permits > requires_or_promotes; (b) highest_probability.
items.failure_case: A policy that bans public chatbots in part 1 (`prohibits`) and approves the in-house assistant in part 2 (`permits`), with no part coding conditions: priority gives `prohibits`, while a single reader would code `restricts_with_conditions`.

items.basis: No service-area list is ruled (the draft offers three candidates), so no order can be written; areas have no ranking in any candidate. items.basis: Taken from the same part as the scale number it describes (the unit is asked only when a number is stated). items.basis: Four-valued item, so any_yes alone does not say what happens when no part says yes; a priority order covers that. The order mirrors the ruled page-verdict order (S3 a ranks unsettled verdicts above stated absence) and keeps an open signal visible, as the institution rule does for unresolved pages (R-005). Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote. This is the combination across parts for one activity; the separate page-level answer (yes if any activity is yes) is unchanged.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts enter as `unknown` (the downgrade target, R-041), which ranks below every substantive value and above `not_documented`, so any supported answer from another part wins. If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: (a) any_yes, completed with the same fallback order (yes if any part says yes; otherwise unclear > no > not_documented): same effect, different rule type; (b) priority yes > no > unclear > not_documented, so an explicit statement that the safeguard does not apply beats an unsettled mention.

items.failure_case: A press release repeats a vendor's 'up to 40% time saved' line in part 2 (`quantified`), while the institution's own outcome is the staff feedback in part 1 (`qualitative`); the vendor figure wins.

items.basis: A reported incident first (richest first, as outcome_kind), then the folded-in 'discontinuation uncertain' signal, weaker than a reported incident but stronger than none. Activity-level: combines the answers of every part that holds a passage of this same activity, as linked by segmentation; parts without a passage of the activity are not asked and do not vote.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts enter as `unknown` (the downgrade target, R-041), which ranks below every substantive value and above `not_documented`, so any supported answer from another part wins. If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part.
items.alternative: discontinuation_uncertain first, so the signal is never lost when an incident is also reported.
items.failure_case: Part 1 reports a data leak (`qualitative`); part 3 hints the tool was quietly withdrawn (`discontinuation_uncertain`). The combined value keeps the incident and drops the discontinuation signal.

items.basis: Rule type sourced: r2#6 extends the page rule to split pooled Stage 6 evidence ('ordered lists take the first value found'). Order proposed: values that do not merge first, because distinct and unresolved relations never merge and merging needs an explicit relation (R-005); among links, the more specific structural link before plain same-activity. Depends on the draft relation list (including how direction is handled). Pair-level answer: each part holds a slice of the two activities' pooled quotes.
items.probability: Producing part's chosen-answer probability and quote: the part whose value won; if several parts gave the winning value, the one with the highest chosen-answer probability (ties: earliest part).
items.downgraded_parts: Downgraded parts enter as `unknown` (the downgrade target, R-041), which ranks below every substantive value and above `not_documented`, so any supported answer from another part wins. If every part is downgraded or silent, the combined answer is `unknown` with the support status of the highest-probability downgraded part. A downgraded `same_activity` therefore never merges.
items.alternative: highest_probability.
items.failure_case: When a pool is split, a part may hold quotes from only one of the two activities and so answers `distinct_action` or `unresolved` by default; that part then blocks a merge the other parts support. A same-versus-distinct conflict also gives `distinct_action`, not `unresolved`.

disagreements_with_preset.issue: The item reads yes = the page holds all information. any_yes then makes the page complete if any one part says complete, the reverse of the round-1 X16 wording ('completeness incomplete' under any-yes). Proposed: complete only if every part says complete (any part `no` gives `no`). Also: every part but the last ends at a cut, so the per-part question must ignore the cut.

disagreements_with_preset.item: core.disclosure_form, core.disclosure_scope (and the first_section items in this draft)
disagreements_with_preset.issue: A gap rather than a disagreement: 'first section' does not say what happens when the first part is silent or downgraded. Proposed convention: the first part with a supported substantive answer. Over pooled Stage 6 evidence, 'first' needs a fixed pool order (for example by source date, then page order).
The table order has no place for `unknown`, the downgrade target. Proposed: `unknown` just above `not_documented`, as in the other orders here.

Agreed. Note: a downgraded verdict keeps its value (r2#40), so a downgraded `confirms_activity` in one part outranks supported negative verdicts in all other parts, and the combined page is downgraded (unresolved for the institution rule). Conservative and seemingly intended; confirm. Alternative: rank supported verdicts before downgraded ones.
